discovery: Discovery of topological insulators and the experimental realization of the quantum anomalous Hall effect

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, China

motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can turn an ordinary insulator into a new phase of matter, the Z2 topological insulator, carrying protected edge or surface states. This introduced band topology as a classification principle for all crystalline solids and launched the field of topological materials, from three-dimensional topological insulators to Dirac and Weyl semimetals. Qi-Kun Xue turned the idea into dissipationless quantum transport. Using molecular-beam epitaxy with atomic-level control of magnetically doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films, his team observed in 2013 the quantum anomalous Hall effect: Hall resistance quantized at h/e^2 with no external magnetic field, a topological state that theory had predicted. It has been reproduced worldwide and now underpins axion-insulator, chiral-Majorana and metrology research. Together these achievements run from a fundamental theoretical concept to its precise realization in the laboratory, and they changed how we understand and design quantum materials.
